Cambodian Movements Detected Near Thai Border Amid Ongoing Tensions

The Second Army Region has reported renewed activity along the Thai-Cambodian border, with several Cambodian trucks and vehicles detected entering certain areas on August 19, 2025.

In its 14:00 briefing, Second Army Region Operations Center confirmed that 23 drones were also spotted operating inside Cambodian territory. Both sides continue to hold their defensive positions, while Thai forces maintain surveillance posts to monitor movements and remain ready to respond if necessary.

Civilian evacuations are ongoing, with 638 residents relocated from high-risk areas in Ubon Ratchathani Province to eight temporary shelters. Local security units have been deployed to safeguard evacuated villages and property.

An Interim Observer Team (IOT) comprising representatives from eight ASEAN nations — Brunei, Malaysia, Laos, Indonesia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, and Vietnam — conducted inspections in Ubon Ratchathani and Sisaket Provinces. Led by Major General Shamsul Rizal bin Musa, Malaysia’s Assistant Defense Attaché to Thailand, the team examined claims of Cambodian ceasefire violations, particularly at Chong Arn Ma–Pha Mo I Daeng, where Cambodian forces reportedly crossed into Thai territory and dismantled barbed wire barriers.

The delegation spent nearly an hour at Chong Arn Ma, observing structural damage to shops and signs of fire and explosions caused by earlier clashes. The site, once a temporary trade crossing, is now a heavily monitored area. Thai officials explained that the Cambodian side of the border previously hosted a UNHCR refugee camp but has since been converted into a casino. Both armies currently maintain unarmed positions in the area under ceasefire terms.

Relief operations are being carried out simultaneously. The Royal Volunteer Command Center units, along with the 25th Military District, distributed survival kits to affected families in Surin Province. University students from Surin Rajabhat University also donated learning materials and supplies to support displaced youth and border communities.

In Ubon Ratchathani, the Deputy Governor and the Thai Red Cross delivered essential items to displaced residents in Nam Yuen and Det Udom districts. Officials visited temporary shelters across eight evacuation centers to provide aid and moral support.

The Second Army Region has urged the public to avoid misinformation and refrain from sharing unverified reports. Citizens are encouraged to rely on official government channels for accurate and timely updates regarding the border situation.

#ThailandCambodia #ไทยรัฐออนไลน์

Just saying 

3.5% rule is a concept in political science that states that when 3.5% of the population of a country protests nonviolently against a government, that government is likely to fall from power.

In 1986, millions of Filipinos took to the streets of Manila in peaceful protest and prayer in the People Power movement. The Marcos regime folded on the fourth day.
In 2003, the people of Georgia ousted Eduard Shevardnadze through the bloodless Rose Revolution, in which protestors stormed the parliament building holding the flowers in their hands. While in 2019, the presidents of Sudan and Algeria both announced they would step aside after decades in office, thanks to peaceful campaigns of resistance.
